summary: EA Sports BIG's arcade street-basketball series; NBA Street V3 is already represented in the Mario archive because of the GameCube Mario cameo version, so this block adds the remaining non-duplicate NBA Street entries.

emulation.notes: Use PCSX2 for the PS2 primary route.

primary.why: The first NBA Street launched on PlayStation 2 before the GameCube port; the PS2 version preserves the original City Circuit structure before the later GameCube version altered the Michael Jordan final-challenge placement.
primary.how_to_play: Play the PS2 version on original hardware or PCSX2 with internal-resolution scaling; use GameCube only for comparison.

emulation.notes: Use Xbox route when compatible; PS2 is a reliable fallback.

primary.why: Vol. 2 shipped on PS2, GameCube, and Xbox with the same core 3-on-3 streetball package; Xbox is selected as the highest-fidelity sixth-generation console route while preserving the full Michael Jordan/NBA legends package.
primary.how_to_play: Play on original Xbox hardware or Xemu if compatible; PS2 via PCSX2 is the fallback route.

emulation.notes: Use PPSSPP for cleaner handheld output.

primary.why: Showdown is the PSP handheld port/spin-off of NBA Street V3, with portable modes, minigames, and ad-hoc multiplayer.
primary.how_to_play: Play on PSP hardware or PPSSPP with internal-resolution scaling.

emulation.notes: Use original Xbox 360 hardware where emulation compatibility is uncertain.

primary.why: Homecourt released on Xbox 360 and PlayStation 3, and the Xbox 360 version is documented as the first Xbox 360 game natively rendered at 1080p.
primary.how_to_play: Play on Xbox 360 hardware or a compatible preservation setup; use PS3 if that is the available HD console route.

primary.why: NBA Street Online was a 2008 South Korean online game, but there is not enough platform/service detail available for a researched release row.
primary.how_to_play: Leave as needs-research until service platform, dates, and current availability are established.
